deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page is working material for Riemann's 1861 memoir 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines gleichartigen flüssigen Ellipsoides', which treats the Dirichlet–Dedekind–Riemann self-gravitating fluid ellipsoid. The page has two parts: (I) the reduced equations of motion for the semi-axes and the start of a linear stability analysis; (II) closed-form evaluation of the spheroidal elliptic integrals needed when two axes are equal.

(I) EQUATIONS OF MOTION.
- Riemann introduces the conserved quantities τ = (b−a)²v and τ' = (b+a)²w'. Here v and w' are his combinations of angular velocity and internal vorticity in the a–b plane.
- The axis equations are
  τ²/(a−b)³ + τ'²/(a+b)³ − ½a'' = εAa − σ/a,
  τ²/(b−a)³ + τ'²/(b+a)³ − ½b'' = εBb − σ/b,
  −½c'' = εCc − σ/c.
  Here σ is the pressure multiplier and A, B, C are the coefficients of the interior potential, with abc = 1 and Δ = √((a²+s)(b²+s)(c²+s)). In this normalisation A = π∫ds/((a²+s)Δ), and similarly for B and C.
- From the c-equation, σ/c = εCc + ½c''. Eliminating σ gives
  εAa − σ/a = εAa − εCc²/a − ½(c/a)c'',
  and the analogous expression for b.
- Energy integral: ½(a'²+b'²+c'²) + τ²/(a−b)² + τ'²/(a+b)² = 2εH + const. [Mine:] differentiating and using a'/a + b'/b + c'/c = 0 confirms this, with dH = −(Aa da + Bb db + Cc dc).
- Partial fractions give
  Aa − Cc²/a = (π/a)∫(ds/Δ)(a²−c²)s/((a²+s)(c²+s)),
  and similarly for b.
- Subtracting the a-equation from the b-equation:
  2τ²/(επ(b−a)³) = p + ½(b−a)''/(επ) + ½((b−a)c/(ab))c''/(επ).
  Here επp = (επ/b)∫…(b²−c²) − (επ/a)∫…(a²−c²).
- Adding them:
  2τ'²/(επ(b+a)³) = q + ½(b+a)''/(επ) + ½((b+a)c/(ab))c''/(επ).

STABILITY SETUP.
- Riemann specialises to c = a, abc = 1, b = a^{−2}, i.e. a spheroid whose distinct axis is b.
- Incompressibility gives δa/a + δb/b + δc/c = 0, hence −δc = δa + a³δb. This is split into the symmetric part (δa+δb) and the antisymmetric part (δb−δa).
- He then linearises the p- and q-equations about equilibrium, with perturbations varying like e^{iμt}, so that d²/dt² → −μ² (normalisations absorbed into μμ). Varying 2τ²/(b−a)³ = p gives 3p(δb−δa)/(b−a) + δa(p_a − (c/a)p_c) + δb(p_b − (c/b)p_c) − μμ(δb−δa) + ((b−a)/(ab))c²μμ(δb/b + δa/a). There is an analogous line for q, written only in part.
- The dispersion relation is not completed on this page.

(II) SPHEROIDAL INTEGRALS.
- Define f(t) = ∫₀^∞ ds/(√(t²+s)(1+s)). The substitution s → t²s shows this equals ∫₀^∞ t ds/(√(1+s)(1+t²s)).
- Set t = cosh y and u = sinh y, so t² − u² = 1 (Riemann writes 'cos' but means cosh). Then f(t) = 2y/u. [Mine:] with w = √(t²+s) the integral is ∫_t^∞ 2dw/(w²−u²) = (1/u)log((t+u)/(t−u)) = 2y/u.
- ∂ denotes d/d log t. With z = t/u = coth y one has d log t/dy = 1/z, dz/dy = 1 − z², d log z/dy = 1/z − z, and ∂ = z d/dy. Also t f(t) = 2yz.
- Define h = ∫ s ds/(√(1+s)(t^{−2}+s)²) = ∫ t s ds/(√(t²+s)(1+s)²).
  From ∂(f/t) = −2h/t² one gets h = −t²∂(yz/t²) = −z² + y(z + z³).
- Differentiating:
  h' = ∂h = −z² + 3z⁴ + y(z + 2z³ − 3z⁵) = ∫ 4t^{−2}s ds/(√(1+s)(t^{−2}+s)³).
- Define g = h' − h = 3z⁴ + y(z³ − 3z⁵). This satisfies g/t = ∂(h/t) = −∫ t² s ds/((t²+s)^{3/2}(1+s)²) = −∫ t³ s ds/((1+s)^{3/2}(1+t²s)²).
- Next:
  g' = ∂g = 13z⁴ − 15z⁶ + y(3z³ − 18z⁵ + 15z⁷) = −4∫ t^{−2}s ds/((1+s)^{3/2}(t^{−2}+s)³),
  g' − 3g = 4z⁴ − 15z⁶ + y(−9z⁵ + 15z⁷) = t³∂(t^{−3}g).
- Margin identity from partial fractions, (s+1) − (s+t^{−2}) = 1 − t^{−2}:
  (1 − 1/t²)g' = −h' − 4g/t².
  Since 1 − 1/t² = 1/z² and z²/t² = z² − 1, this becomes g' = −z²h' − 4g(z² − 1). It checks against the explicit formulas.
- Finally, everything is converted to the spheroid variable t = b/a = a^{−3}, i.e. t^{−2} = a⁶, via s → a⁴s. For example, g' = −4∫ a^{−4}s ds/((1+a⁴s)^{3/2}(1+s/a²)³). These are exactly the integrals A, B, C and their derivatives entering p_a, p_b, p_c for the case c = a, b = a^{−2}.
errors: The decomposition δa + a³δb = ½(δa+δb)(a³+1) + (δb−δa)(a³−1) holds only if the ½ also multiplies the second term. Either a slip, or the ½ multiplies a bracket enclosing both terms (the image suggests a closing parenthesis).
In the line deriving h, the intermediate expression '(z+y(1−zz))z + 2yz' has the wrong sign as written: it should be −(z+y(1−zz))z + 2yz. The final result h = −z² + y(z+z³) is correct.
The a-form of h' appears without the factor 4. Correct: h' = ∫ 4a^{−4}s ds/(√(1+a⁴s)(1+s/a²)³). This is a slip or a transcription issue.
For t³∂(t^{−3}g) = g' − 3g, the correct integral is 3∫ t⁵ s ds/((t²+s)^{5/2}(1+s)²) = 3∫ a^{−4}s ds/((1+a⁴s)^{5/2}(1+s/a²)²). The exponent written/transcribed as 3/2 should be 5/2.
Riemann writes t = cos y, but the relations dt/dy = u, du/dy = t and tt − uu = 1 require t = cosh y, u = sinh y.
Normalisation factors of ½ and επ in the linearised equations are absorbed into μμ without comment. This is internally consistent but not stated.

results.what: Reduced equations of motion for the semi-axes of a self-gravitating fluid ellipsoid with conserved quantities τ = (b−a)²v, τ' = (b+a)²w', pressure eliminated, and the energy integral
Partial-fraction form of Aa − Cc²/a as an integral, and the difference/sum equations defining p and q
results.modern_name: Index symbols / Chandrasekhar's A_i, A_ij relations

results.what: Linearised (second-variation) equations about an equilibrium spheroid c = a, b = a^{−2}, using the incompressibility constraint
results.modern_name: Linear stability analysis of Riemann ellipsoids (the second-order virial method is the later systematic version)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1861 (his stability treatment was later corrected by Lebovitz and Chandrasekhar, 1960s)

results.what: Closed-form evaluation of spheroidal integrals: f(t) = 2y/u with t = cosh y, h = −z² + y(z+z³), g = 3z⁴ + y(z³−3z⁵), g' etc., with z = coth y, and the recursion g' = −z²h' − 4(z²−1)g
results.modern_name: Elementary (logarithmic/hyperbolic) evaluation of the index-symbol integrals for spheroids

deep.surprise_reason: This is draft computation for Riemann's published 1861 fluid-ellipsoid paper: equations of motion, the energy integral and stability setup, plus classical closed-form spheroid integrals. All of it is either published by Riemann or classical. It is of interest only as a detail of his working method for the stability analysis.

transcription_corrections: 't = cos y' should be read as t = cosh y (u = sinh y), since tt − uu = 1.
h = ∫ t⁴ ∂s/(√(tt+s)(1+s)²) should be h = ∫ t s ∂s/(√(tt+s)(1+s)²).
'∂t ∂(1/t)h' line: the operator is ∂ = d/d log t applied to g = t∂(h/t); the result is g'.
'∂t³g' should read ∂(t^{−3}g) = t^{−3}(g'−3g), with the integrand exponent (tt+s)^{5/2}, not 3/2, if written correctly.
The a-form of h' should carry a factor 4: ∫ 4a^{−4}s∂s/(√(1+a⁴s)(1+s/aa)³).
Margin 'g' = −zz(h'+4g)' is more plausibly g' = −zz(h' + 4g/tt), equivalent to g' = −h'z² − 4g(z²−1).
'∂ log t/∂y − ∂ log u/∂y = 1/z' is better read as = 1/z − z or similar; the clean relations are ∂log t/∂y = 1/z and ∂log z/∂y = 1/z − z.
The margin log expression is probably log((1+√(1−1/t))/(1−√(1−1/t))) or similar, an alternative closed form of the same integral; uncertain.
